newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends weaker on Kia, DMZ skirmish.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends weaker on Kia, DMZ skirmish.

text.p: The won ended weaker against the dollar on Wednesday on fears of tightening dollar supply following local banks' decision to bail out the troubled Kia Group, dealers said.
Dealers said skirmishes on the Demilitarized Zone between North and South Korea on Wednesday also pushed foreign banks in Seoul to sell wons for dollars.
The won finished at 893.50, down from Tuesday's close of 891.90 despite five interventions by the central bank to support the won.

"It will not be easy to dampen the strong buying sentiment as there are concerns dollar supplies will tighten as borrowing from abroad becomes more difficult after Kia's troubles," said a dealer at Korea First Bank.
Another local bank dealer said the won could weaken to the 895 level on Friday and further intervention from the Bank of Korea should be expected.
Friday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 892.80 from 890.80 today. The market will be closed on Thursday for Constitutional Day.
